mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate level (as measured by the current value) is causally linked to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate cash flows.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for FEDFUNDS level as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return in the lowest FEDFUNDS quartile is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 5.0%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day S&P 500 return when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the threshold signal is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and retail sales indicates robust consumer spending, which boosts corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the interaction term (HOUST and RSAFS both rising) as a predictor of 60-day S&P 500 returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 60-day return when both series rise is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), weak labor market conditions suppress consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day S&P 500 return when UNRATE > 5.0% is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the UNRATE threshold signal is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (as measured by the current value) signals robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate output and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for INDPRO level as a predictor of 60-day S&P 500 returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between INDPRO level and 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly payroll growth exceeds 135,000 thousand, it indicates a tight labor market that fuels consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day S&P 500 return when PAYEMS > 135000 is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the PAYEMS threshold signal is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) signals a late-cycle economic regime with tightening monetary policy and labor market overheating, which precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the interaction term (FEDFUNDS > 5.0% AND UNRATE < 4.0%) as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return when both conditions hold is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In low industrial production regimes (INDPRO < 100), weak manufacturing activity indicates a slowing economy that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day S&P 500 return when INDPRO < 100 is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the INDPRO threshold signal is less than 0.03.
